title: Units regulators and hR validation
objective: Implement rigorous outward Arb enclosure transport, precision-safe regulator refinement, bounded exact unit p-saturation, and adaptive analytic retry hooks

exceptions: The existing FLINT Node-API host adapter must export exact Arb dyadic endpoints; ordinary Python consumes that proof boundary and fails closed when the native capability is absent.

handoff.summary: Fixed the regulator refinement precision intersection and replaced decimal midpoint/radius proof transport with exact outward dyadic endpoints obtained from Arb. Added a bounded exact unit p-saturation producer with replayable p-th-root identities, exact maximal-order/unit checks, index-p basis replacement, adaptive reconstruction retry, finite-order-quotient negative obstructions, canonical evidence serialization, and a fail-closed result state. Real quadratic runtime checks cover enlargement, tamper rejection, untrusted bounds, bounded-search incompleteness, local obstruction completion, and doubled-precision retry.
risks: Rigorous zeta status assumes the caller supplies the actual maximal-order discriminant and a complete exact splitting provider; the function validates prime coverage and every local degree identity but does not independently prove the field/order identity.

The p-th-root producer is intentionally bounded by an order-coordinate box and candidate cap. Missing roots outside that box never certify saturation; completion then requires exhaustive finite-quotient obstructions for every exponent/torsion target or exhaustion of a rigorously supplied global index.

Only algebraic logarithm inputs cross the corrected Arb endpoint boundary. Determinant and zeta transcendental evaluation remain explicitly typed exact-rational intervals with mpmath.libmp directed rounding, not Arb balls.

FactoredNumberFieldElement currently exposes only scalar qqbarLogAbsBall calls. The measured strict-Python regulator determinant is already sub-millisecond for the rank-two fixture, while zeta finite-interval evaluation dominated the profile, so this lane did not add an unmeasured algebraic-log batch boundary.

The corrected C source passes a direct syntax check against FLINT headers, but the lane's direct addon rebuild is blocked by a pre-existing shared native artifact lacking NTL headers. The package-local native transport test and broad native gate remain for central integration.
next_steps: Wire ExactUnitSaturationResult into the class/unit engine using the full rigorous HRIndexValidationResult, retain its canonical evidence payload in map proofs, and replay verify_saturation_record rather than trusting stage labels.
Rebuild the FLINT addon in central integration, run the claimed top-level context test against the new endpoint payload, then run pnpm test:native before moving this contract to review.
